about: Every resource the process view draws, loaded on one process in phases whose values are known: a function that dominates the cpu, a sleep, a lock another thread holds, a resident footprint touched page by page, a file written and fsynced to a disk, and bytes exchanged with a child over loopback -- each a line of the process view, which the dedicated views explain.

phases.what: `crunch` then `tidy`, five rounds, on the main thread
`queue_up` waits for the lock `process-holder` sleeps under
32 MiB touched a page at a time, held to the end
`process.bin` written in 64 KiB writes and fsynced
1 MiB sent to `process-peer` over loopback, then 256 KiB received
the footprint held while the program idles

trust.cpu: exact to a few microseconds on the main thread's cpu clock: `crunch` four times `tidy`, together 0.75 s; a profile sees them within its sampling error
trust.sleep: at least what was asked, longer by the scheduler's slack
trust.lock: the holder sleeps `seconds` under the lock; the main thread waits that long less a few hundred microseconds
trust.memory: the resident size grows by at least `bytes` and stays there to the end, `hold_s` after the last of the rest, so a poll of the resident size sees it
trust.file: exact at the system calls, on descriptor `fd`

not_exercised.GPU: a Python program launches no kernel without a GPU library this repository does not depend on; the line reads `no kernel launched` (the `lanes` workload launches `spin` kernels where there is a device)
not_exercised.Energy: the machine's draw is not the workload's to set: the line reads the machine's `power.energy`, apportioned by the busy cores' share only where the machine's cores are known (a live run)
not_exercised.capacity: a recording does not carry its machine's cores or memory, so CPU and Memory are drawn in the neutral hue there; a live run colours them by the share of the machine
